A definitive verdict requires relevant cited changed code and documentation, complete coverage, sufficient context and no unresolved applicability.

decisions.reason: Protects local state while making intentional graph sharing predictable.
decisions.text: Keep the shareable graph, rather than local execution state, under version control. Read-only queries do not rewrite the snapshot; export when reusable knowledge changes. Invalid snapshots or symbolic-link paths fail without replacing local knowledge.

decisions.reason: Sets product and documentation ownership boundaries.
decisions.text: Projects use a small versioned source configuration. Hivex does not create private agent memory, a hosted documentation database, or another session orchestrator; Hivex documentation stays in its repository and project-specific language and decisions stay in the project’s documentation.

conditions: Explicit updates can advance remaining rounds. A completed consultation can be reused only while its supplied context is unchanged.
exceptions: Increasing the context limit does not reset an unfinished work item's budget.
decisions.reason: Provides useful incremental consultation without requiring full-corpus processing before an answer.
decisions.text: Before answering a consultation, maintain at most one bounded pending batch, prioritizing matching fragments and known affected neighbors. Update, check, and answer share one work budget; remaining corpus coverage stays visible.

conditions: The directory distinction is an adoption default.
exceptions: An existing arrangement may remain where migration would not be appropriate.
decisions.reason: Keeps document collections understandable without forcing needless restructuring.
decisions.text: Use guidelines for standing rules and design guidance, and procedures for carrying out tasks; avoid overlapping directories with indistinct purposes. These organization choices are defaults, not a reason to migrate an existing arrangement when migration is inappropriate.

conditions: The finding, candidate, check, graph, and sources must match the retained check; unsupported targets and structural failures remain blocking.
exceptions: This path does not apply to real candidate defects, which require correction or repair.
decisions.reason: Allows a narrowly scoped review of a false finding without erasing adverse evidence or bypassing source checks.
decisions.text: A false semantic finding on a retained repair candidate may be reviewed locally against its exact work, check input, and current canonical candidate, using a bounded reason and current versioned evidence. The operation makes no model call and leaves the original finding, check, candidate, attempt, receipts, budget, and consumption intact. A review closure is a source-backed judgment, not proof of correctness; do not use it to disposition a real contradiction or missing dependency.

conditions: Migration is preferred when reasonably possible.
exceptions: An existing layout may remain; organization is not required for ingestion.
decisions.reason: Encourages useful organization without making migration a condition of use.
decisions.text: For adoption, prefer migration to the recommended structure when reasonably possible while preserving useful documents, authority, history, and links. Other Markdown layouts remain readable and are not an ingestion prerequisite.

exceptions: The implementing agent may use a different model.
decisions.reason: Describes the current default and shipped integration without making that model a permanent product requirement.
decisions.text: The current default knowledge profile is GPT-6 Luna at max effort through Codex; Codex is the only shipped execution integration. An implementing agent may use another model.

conditions: The selected profile is the one validated for this release.
exceptions: The release choice does not prohibit configuring another supported model for another user; do not build a provider framework speculatively.
decisions.reason: Makes current model selection explicit without making it an unchangeable product requirement.
decisions.text: For the validated release, use the owner's selected Luna/max knowledge profile without silent fallback, while keeping model selection localized so another user can configure a supported model.

decisions.reason: Protects revision consistency and prevents incomplete evidence from being presented as complete.
decisions.text: Search and read must refer to the same immutable revision. The index is disposable derived data, initially built in memory for each search. Reads return complete Markdown blocks or an explicit continuation or error, never silently truncate a condition to fit a budget; previews do not certify evidence sufficiency.

conditions: The selected model and options must be supported by the integration.
The work ID, operation, source versions, and arguments must match the retained work.
exceptions: Profile selection cannot change scope or completed work.
Running or unresolved uncertain invocations cannot be resumed this way.
decisions.reason: Keep integration/profile selection and retained-work continuity together: enforce the admitted provider boundary while preserving scope, cumulative accounting and provenance.
decisions.text: Integration and model selection are independent. `--integration` selects the connection; `--model` and `--effort` select a profile supported by that connection. Codex currently admits OpenAI through ChatGPT, so other `--model-provider` values and uninstalled integrations fail explicitly. Provider-specific options and authentication belong to their integration. A future integration can use different model options without requiring a reasoning level named `max`. Continuing retained work with a non-default profile requires an explicit profile-resumption choice under the same work, operation, source versions, and original arguments. Recording that choice alone does not invoke the model or relabel completed work; repeated identical choices are idempotent. Reject changed sources, unknown work IDs, ambiguous ownership, running or unresolved uncertain invocations; failed work still needs explicit retry and ordinary recovery remains required. Each work records its requested profile and receipts record the observed effective profile when known. profileReplacement preserves the previous profile/request identity and current choice, while previousReplacements keeps earlier transitions. Coverage follows the same work atomically; decision and relationship IDs, evidence, quality, raw results and receipts retain provenance. A changed candidate requires its normal check under the chosen profile within the same cumulative allowance; selection never repeats an unchanged adverse check.

decisions.reason: Makes the scope of knowledge consultation and implementation review version-specific.
decisions.text: Task context is the relevant decisions, evidence, and uncertainties. An implementation version captures changes against a particular base and the exact contents of affected files; later changes are outside that version. A finding is a possible conflict between implementation and project knowledge, which the principal reviewer verifies while retaining review responsibility.

conditions: Identical request arguments are coalesced; different references resolving to the same file revision are rejected.
decisions.reason: Keeps contextual code versioned and distinct from the changed code being reviewed.
decisions.text: Optional contextual code must come from explicit Git revision/path pairs as complete regular UTF-8 blobs; do not follow filesystem symlinks or infer files. Retain reference, resolved commit, path, mode and blob ID, and invalidate evidence if a moving reference changes during execution or revalidation. Use separate context citations for context files and before/after citations for changed implementation; reference code cannot substitute for citing the changed implementation.

conditions: Add a second review when concrete risk or findings warrant it.
Use model assistance when it adds value.
exceptions: One independent review is the default; a second is not compulsory.
decisions.reason: Adapts review and knowledge assistance to risk while preserving work history and budget.
decisions.text: Use one independent review by default; add another when concrete risk or findings warrant it. The reviewer uses the implementer's model and effort, while knowledge assistance remains a separate role. Begin knowledge assistance with local retrieval and source reading, and call the model when it adds value. Preserve budget, history, and uncertainty rather than rerunning work to obtain approval.

conditions: Resolve active warnings against current sources and keep current-source ingestion/checks and dependencies fresh before integration.
Recheck freshness after later source edits.
A deferred capability may be dispositioned only while its authority prohibits implementation or activation until prerequisites are met.
exceptions: A native partial result or historical reference alone does not establish a current defect.
decisions.reason: Sets the knowledge-before-merge gate while distinguishing current blockers from historical or native quality markings.
decisions.text: Adopting projects must maintain valuable Markdown and its derived graph before integration, resolve active warnings with evidence, and leave no pending current-source ingestion or checks or stale/unavailable current dependencies. Keep changes in the owning authority and export the graph with its Markdown; later source edits require renewed freshness checks. A native partial result alone is not a current defect: historical references and native quality marks may remain after review. The independent reviewer records a disposition against current sources without deleting history, promoting native quality, or repeating checks merely for a green label. Actual contradictions, missing decisions needed by supported behavior, and uncertain execution still block. A deferred capability may be dispositioned while its authority prohibits implementation or activation until prerequisites are met; roadmap inclusion alone does not make it supported behavior, and being unrelated to one PR is not sufficient.

conditions: The model is invoked only after inputs pass validation.
exceptions: The preparation operation does not invoke the model.
decisions.reason: Makes review provenance and request contents verifiable without omitting source material.
decisions.text: Bind each result to the exact graph hash, source revision and content, prompt and schema, admitted native profile, and measured usage. Reject stale or oversized input before model invocation and do not truncate sources. Preparation exposes the exact bounded request without invoking the model.

conditions: A corrected local admission rule may reassess an unchanged retained check without another model call only after verifying candidate identity, evidence freshness, and graph continuity.
exceptions: Preserve the original failed assessment and consumed budget.
decisions.reason: Separates inherited uncertainty from current candidate defects without weakening evidence safeguards.
decisions.text: Replacement admission uses findings from the current check, not inherited neighbor uncertainty as a new rejection. Preserve inherited uncertainty, but reject current findings affecting the relationship or its endpoints and invalid evidence.

conditions: Import is blocked while local work remains unfinished.
exceptions: Work explicitly superseded by a completed reviewed replacement does not block import.
decisions.reason: Protects local progress when adopting shared graph knowledge.
decisions.text: A fresh clone can query a shared snapshot without a local database. When a local graph already exists it takes precedence; importing a shared version requires local work to be completed or recovered and does not reset attempts or budgets. Its first update reuses matching ingestion units and starts local work accounting.

conditions: Use a separate issue only when needed to preserve independently actionable work that cannot be absorbed into the existing ticket.
exceptions: Read-only retrieval does not require a ticket.
A defined change may proceed without additional discovery or a new spec.
decisions.reason: Coordinates tracked execution while keeping durable decisions in the relevant project authority.
decisions.text: Work is issue-first in the owning repository, with design, documentation, implementation, review, and Git used as appropriate. Resolve open decisions through discovery or a grill; add specs or execution tickets when they clarify or divide work, but a defined change may proceed directly to implementation and review. Resolve existing work before changing code and link the PR and verification to it. Absorb findings into the existing ticket where possible; create a separate issue only for independently actionable work that cannot fit, and explain why. Read-only retrieval needs no ticket. A cross-repository parent provides context and coordination, not a replacement for native tracking. Tickets and specs track scope and acceptance; durable decisions belong in the repository's documentary authority.

conditions: Compact an ADR when replaced text obscures its current meaning.
exceptions: Do not archive a live exception; other layouts remain valid.
decisions.reason: Keeps active guidance legible without losing applicable exceptions or historical evidence.
decisions.text: When replaced text obscures a decision's current meaning, keep the active document focused on applicable rules and move history to a clearly marked archive; a wholly superseded ADR may become a pointer. Preserve anchors or update links, keep live exceptions accessible, and do not change what an earlier decision meant. Historical material should remain available for focused consultation.

decisions.reason: Shares reusable knowledge without implying that local execution state is part of the snapshot.
decisions.text: Snapshot export atomically writes stable, readable graph JSON for sharing alongside the Markdown it describes. It exports graph knowledge and provenance, not work records, budgets, or cached answers, and makes no model calls.

decisions.reason: Restore the protected historical-consultation endpoint from an earlier completed original unit, keeping its explicit-selection and evidence boundary distinct from general source fallback.
decisions.text: Historical sources are not included in ordinary consultation merely because they are available; explicit focused selection or a known dependency is required. Report necessary excluded or unavailable historical evidence and unconsulted historical or unavailable local Markdown links for the responsible agent to assess. Linking an archive does not ingest it automatically.

conditions: Run with `cargo test --locked --test quality`.
exceptions: Scores equal to either threshold pass.
decisions.reason: Sets measurable, inclusive complexity limits and a defined analysis scope.
decisions.text: The locked quality test enforces cognitive complexity at most 15 and cyclomatic complexity at most 20; equality passes. It analyzes Rust files under `src`, `tools`, and `tests`, including test code and inactive conditional-compilation branches. It fails on unreadable files, invalid syntax, parse errors, absent or non-finite metrics, or threshold violations, and requires at least one measured implementation function.

conditions: TDD is reserved for critical behavior that is sufficiently defined.
exceptions: TDD is optional even for such critical behavior.
decisions.reason: Keeps testing risk-based without making TDD or other checks a ritual.
decisions.text: Choose tests by concrete value and risk. TDD is optional, including for critical flows, and is reserved for critical behavior that is sufficiently defined. Other checks and tests need concrete value rather than compliance with a testing ritual.

conditions: The choice is consequential and its rationale would otherwise be surprising.
exceptions: Routine edits and dependency choices do not each require an ADR.
decisions.reason: Reserves ADRs for decisions that benefit from durable rationale.
decisions.text: Use an ADR for a consequential architectural trade-off whose rationale would otherwise be surprising, not for every routine edit or dependency.

decisions.reason: Separates deterministic retrieval and validation from model operations.
decisions.text: Retrieval and deterministic validation are model-free.

conditions: Results are committed only for the process that claimed the source.
exceptions: Unresolved invocations are not automatically retried.
decisions.reason: Protects concurrent work and preserves truthful invocation accounting.
decisions.text: Claim each pending source in a short immediate transaction, invoke the model outside it, and atomically commit results only for the claimant. Concurrent processes may work on distinct sources but cannot reclaim claimed or completed work. Record the attempt before invocation and retain available reports and known usage. A crash or persistence failure leaves an unresolved invocation; elapsed time or a missing process does not establish that no request occurred, so unresolved work is not retried automatically. A completed candidate is neither an admitted graph nor a successful grounding.

conditions: Omitted selection arguments resume the recorded plan.
exceptions: An explicit different selection is rejected before a model invocation.
decisions.reason: Preserves the run's source and processing basis across resumptions.
decisions.text: An ingestion run is bound to an immutable plan containing its source commit, collection, configuration, preparation policy, and complete source identities. Omitted selectors resume that plan even if HEAD changes; an explicitly different selection fails before model use. Sources remain in Git and their documentation folders, while the store is not documentary authority.

conditions: Reference definitions retain their original positions, even when outside the selected section; only links located inside the section participate.
exceptions: External destinations and non-Markdown assets are counted but not opened; code examples, images, and raw HTML are not scanned for relationships.
decisions.reason: Makes authored-link selection reproducible while preserving unresolved references and its coverage limits.
decisions.text: Discover candidate pairs deterministically from parsed Markdown links in the selected section of the same graph snapshot. Links suggest comparison, not relationship or precedence; unresolved targets remain explicit, and absent links do not establish independence or full semantic coverage. The plan records graph identity, policy, provenance, pairs, unresolved links, and possible-pair count. Planning makes no model calls or graph changes. Discovery is bounded to 10,000 links or definitions per document, 10,000 inspected links, 32,768 pairs, and 8 MiB; a smaller requested output budget either returns the complete plan or fails.

conditions: Retained diagnostics are integrity-checked and remain within existing result bounds.
exceptions: Rejected output does not establish a review verdict.
decisions.reason: Preserves bounded failure evidence without treating invalid output as semantic evidence.
decisions.text: When fidelity output fails validation, retain its rejected text and hash only as untrusted diagnostics. It is not a partial review or evidence for revision; validate its integrity and invalid-output status, and do not infer a verdict from the error.

conditions: Describes the first native delivery only.
decisions.reason: Preserves the earlier migration state without presenting it as the current toolchain.
decisions.text: The initial native delivery temporarily retained Bun and TypeScript for tests and packaging even after retiring the TypeScript runtime; that transitional development-tool boundary was later amended.

conditions: Comparison and source-review store application identities remain distinct.
A complete export must fit the requested budget and is never truncated.
exceptions: A later command may process other pending pairs, but does not retry or approve a retained negative result.
decisions.reason: Provides bounded, resumable comparison work without conflating it with source-fidelity review or losing evidence.
decisions.text: Retain authored-link comparison cohorts in a local comparisons store bound to the graph, complete selection, and each pair's prompt and processing contract. An empty selection or unresolved link plan cannot succeed. Cohorts support up to 2,048 pairs and a 1 MiB processing plan; the discovery plan has a separate 8 MiB limit. The store is capped at 128 MiB, each result at 8 MiB, and each active or new claim reserves 16 MiB before invocation. Resume pending work without repeating retained results; stop the current loop on a negative or failed result, and leave unknown outcomes unresolved. Export and inspection revalidate evidence and coverage; retirement requires the exact plan hash, rejects unresolved invocations, and is explicit.

conditions: Mappings must cover protected prior relationships with current endpoints and citations, compatible type and direction, sufficient range coverage, and a bounded explanation. A supported dependency that remains distinct requires a replacement; removal is limited to unsupported meaning or meaning fully coalesced in a current decision, with complete evidence.
The reviewer judges semantic equivalence; structural checks and text similarity cannot establish it. Real candidate defects require correction and a fresh check.
exceptions: Keep the adverse check, candidate, attempts, receipts, budgets, and consumption intact; record dispositions separately and make exact replay idempotent. Associated findings need their own evidenced resolution.
decisions.reason: Allows carefully bounded source-backed review of a retained check without turning review into another certification loop.
decisions.text: A source-backed review may dispose of a false relationship finding or supply an omitted replacement mapping for the exact retained check, without re-extraction or another check. Bind the review to the original work, check input, candidate, and supplied source versions.

decisions.reason: Defines the distinct roles of executable evidence and authored documentation.
decisions.text: Code, contracts, and tests explain executable behavior; documentation records intent, language, decisions, and constraints that execution alone cannot explain.

decisions.reason: Makes verification claims specific to the revision and checks performed.
decisions.text: Choose verification for the affected surfaces. Code changes need typechecking, linting, formatting, and relevant behavior tests; documentation-only changes need formatting and checks of affected references or declared sources. Record the exact revision and checks actually completed. A later change invalidates affected results, and omitted, interrupted, or truncated checks must not be reported as passing.

conditions: Applies to pull-request checks and execution of public contributions.
exceptions: Fork approval is an additional control, not an exception to isolated execution.
decisions.reason: Limits the credentials and execution exposure of untrusted contributions.
decisions.text: For pull requests, use read-only repository permissions, do not persist checkout credentials, and provide no publishing credentials or repository secrets. Keep publication separate; do not execute public contributions on a personal workstation or use pull_request_target to check out and run an untrusted branch. Fork approval does not replace isolated execution.

conditions: Remaining coverage stays visible.
exceptions: A completed answer is reusable only for an unchanged task and context.
decisions.reason: Provides bounded, resumable consultation without requiring full-corpus processing first.
decisions.text: Before answering an ask, update at most one bounded batch, prioritizing matching fragments, relevant documents, and known dependencies, then query Luna/max. Update, check, and answer share a default total of three calls. If that allowance ends before an answer, resume the same task with an authorized higher total while retaining progress and consumption. An unchanged task reuses its answer; explicit updates advance remaining corpus coverage.

decisions.reason: Defines the project's readiness-label meanings.
decisions.text: The readiness labels distinguish issues needing evaluation, essential information, agent-ready work, human implementation, and work that will not be actioned.

conditions: The stated runtime independence applies to the installed executable.
exceptions: The package manager, either npm or Bun, is used to install the package.
decisions.reason: Describes the package’s present supported target and runtime boundary without implying other targets are supported.
decisions.text: The installed native package currently targets macOS ARM64; its executable does not need Bun, Node.js, or Rust at runtime. Other targets require native compatibility validation before distribution.

conditions: When providing knowledge support, a handoff, or a definitive finding.
exceptions: Deterministic retrieval and maintenance do not require a model.
decisions.reason: Grounds reusable knowledge and review in verifiable project evidence without making model use universal.
decisions.text: Use repository decisions and review evidence rather than private agent memory; checkpoints identify the exact commit, verified work, and remaining work. Begin with local search, neighbors, and source reading, using model-assisted interpretation or review only when useful. Reviewers verify findings; missing context or uncertainty limits the conclusions, and definitive findings identify the actual document and implementation versions. Knowledge-model operations use the admitted Luna/max profile and record actual usage, including failed or interrupted attempts; deterministic retrieval and maintenance need no model.

conditions: Additional reviewers are warranted by concrete risk or review findings.
A cheaper model may perform routine implementation subtasks only with explicit authorization.
decisions.reason: Keeps code review independent and configured separately from knowledge extraction.
decisions.text: Use one independent code review by default for scope, correctness, and standards; add reviewers when concrete risk or findings justify it. Reviewers use the implementer's model and reasoning effort. If a subagent default differs, pass the intended profile explicitly and verify the effective configuration. Do not use the cheaper knowledge model for code review. A cheaper model may be used for routine implementation subtasks only when explicitly authorized; Hivex knowledge extraction and checking use the user's separately configured knowledge model.

conditions: Revision is supported only by completed adverse fidelity with sufficient context and concrete evidence.
exceptions: Passing or unresolved fidelity cannot support revision.
decisions.reason: Separates new reassessment evidence from retries, existing cohort records, and candidate admission.
decisions.text: Comparison-feedback reassessment is a new evidenced assessment, not a retry or replacement of an existing cohort review; preserve original source reviews and comparisons. Only a completed adverse fidelity finding that meets the existing context and evidence requirements may support candidate revision. Passing or unresolved fidelity cannot do so. The candidate remains unaccepted and requires ordinary fresh fidelity review before admission; revalidate feedback and request bindings when consuming the result.

decisions.reason: Defines the shared knowledge artifact and its evidence boundary.
decisions.text: `.hivex/graph.json` is the portable, Git-suitable knowledge snapshot: it contains reusable graph knowledge, source versions, evidence, provenance, and coverage or uncertainty information. Preserve known provenance and identify unavailable legacy metadata; do not invent it.

conditions: Source-assessment reuse validates current graph binding and equality of the original source-review inputs.
Pair-comparison reuse validates graph and selection association and equality of complete pair inputs and source/claim bindings.
exceptions: Reuse does not constitute a new model call.
decisions.reason: Prevents reused evidence from being misapplied to changed graph or comparison inputs.
decisions.text: Reuse source assessments and pair comparisons only with their complete original results or receipts and explicit associations to the current graph and selection. Validate current bindings and equality of original inputs, including source and claim bindings, while retaining original identities. Reuse is not a new model call and cannot extend a pair assessment beyond its two sources.

conditions: The candidate, source-bound graph, review evidence, and source descriptor must meet the stated matching and completeness requirements.
exceptions: A passing, unresolved, insufficient-context, or uncertain review cannot trigger revision.
decisions.reason: Restricts semantic revision to sufficiently grounded adverse evidence tied to the actual source revision.
decisions.text: Semantic revision requires the exact retained candidate and its source-bound graph, plus a validated adverse fidelity result with sufficient context. The review must retain a completed admitted invocation, literal evidence, and complete claim and relation coverage. Passing reviews, unresolved findings, insufficient context, or uncertain invocations do not qualify. An export may supply the selected result but does not approve other rows. The graph snapshot and full source descriptor, including authority and processing inputs, must match the frozen plan; resolve the model's source from that plan because candidate and receipt hashes alone do not establish which revision the invocation could read.

conditions: Applies when running `hivex init`.
decisions.reason: Makes skill installation repeatable while avoiding writes through unsafe parent links.
decisions.text: Initialization links the bundled skills into the documented agent skill locations, preserves existing skill directories and links, and rejects parent-directory symlinks before writing files.

conditions: These requirements applied to admission of a graph rebuild.
decisions.reason: The supplied guide says the earlier candidate, fidelity, comparison, and admission protocols were retired from the active CLI.
decisions.text: The earlier graph-rebuild admission path required a frozen source cohort and processing contract, provenance, structural checks, and semantic evaluation; changed sources, parsing, or extraction inputs required an explicit cache or gold disposition before rebuild.

conditions: A demonstrated contradiction must be corrected or resolved through an approved decision change.
An unresolved question escalated to the owner includes sources, impact, and a recommendation.
exceptions: Hivex does not perform every aspect of code review or rewrite Markdown itself.
decisions.reason: Supports autonomous work without transferring implementation acceptance or documentary authority to Hivex.
decisions.text: The implementing agent consults Hivex before coherent feature or behavior changes; the principal reviewer consults it with the task and diff, verifies findings, and remains responsible for accepting the implementation. Apply settled decisions autonomously and ask the owner only after available evidence and tools cannot resolve the issue.

conditions: The compatibility statement applies to the verified macOS ARM64 target.
exceptions: It does not claim compatibility for other platforms that could previously install the Bun package.
decisions.reason: Records the native artifact’s actual target and distribution shape without extending its compatibility claim.
decisions.text: The native distribution currently retains the scoped package, command, six skills, and optional language templates. Its first verified native target is macOS ARM64; npm links directly to the executable without a JavaScript launcher, runtime package dependency, or installation hook, and the package declares its OS and CPU.

decisions.reason: Prevents synthetic test results from being mistaken for real usage measurements.
decisions.text: Real Luna evaluations are bounded and reported separately from simulated tests; simulated token usage is not a measure of actual consumption. Development is issue-first, with coherent pull requests, an independent review covering scope, correctness and standards, and CI on the final commit. Earlier candidate/fidelity/comparison/admission protocols and their tests are retired from the active CLI. Their code remains in Git history and historical evidence keeps its original results. They do not impose a requirement to reproduce an Opus graph or exhaustively replay an old gold suite.

conditions: Each bounded update batch has one additional knowledge check; avoid per-node or exhaustive source-pair review.
exceptions: Useful knowledge remains available when another part is pending or uncertain, with those limits visible; correct derived interpretations against sources without changing doctrine.
decisions.reason: Limits unnecessary certification work while preserving resumability and source traceability.
decisions.text: Process updates in bounded, source-bound units and rounds, preserving original line provenance and checkpointing progress for resumption. Reuse extraction only when the source and processing context still match; caches have no authority.

relationships.reason: Current Guide 46 decision a722f35e requires migration to preserve useful material and forbids semantic source rewrites; current ADR 0010:11–13 decision a1ee5d41 makes Markdown authoritative. These roles preserve the supports relationship.
The guide’s archive-building procedure applies the separation between native artifact verification and registry release.
Work-budget accounting spans attempts, whose definition specifies that failed and unknown-usage invocations remain accounted for across resumption.
The engineering responsibility split assigns workflow policy to Markdown and knowledge state to the CLI, consistent with Markdown remaining the source and the graph remaining derived.
The report describes warnings produced by the normal warning-maintenance check.
Test placement by parser and integration contract applies validation at the public CLI and protocol seam.
Semantic revision requires a complete, validated, sufficiently contextualized fidelity result; a successful review alone does not admit a graph.
Keeping the graph focused on meaningful decisions, dependencies, and exceptions implements the semantic-graph and retrieval contract.
The selected knowledge profile is an instance of the separate, configurable execution-profile rule.
A grounded claim needs the selected documentary context and must expose when that context is insufficient.
Atomic reuse validation applies to the explicit archive-based transition.
A consultation's update, check, and answer must share the operation-wide budget and resumption accounting.
Final relationship disposition depends on retaining the old relationship and provenance until its dependent units are processed.
The current Rust development direction also retires the historical Bun-specific installation approach.
Consistent application of the tracker labels depends on their defined meanings.
Focused archive use follows the configured boundary that keeps historical sources out of ordinary ingestion.
Lexical neighbors extend candidate selection while retaining the authored-link plan and its unresolved-link constraints.
An explicitly selected continuation profile must be validated by the chosen integration without silent fallback.
Distinguishing shared from scope-specific knowledge supports context-specific glossaries linked to shared material.
Validly superseded work explicitly no longer blocks relocation, which otherwise refuses unfinished local work.
Focused archived work shares the consultation’s bounded resumable-work budget.
The reassessment workflow supplies the separately validated adverse fidelity evidence that may support revision under the existing conditions.
Reviewing new and reopened warnings depends on the reviewer evidence duties.
The engineering guidance that repository Markdown remains human-maintained authority reinforces the distinction between source documents and derived graph knowledge.
Protected relationship mappings are a specialized form of the same exact retained-check, source-backed false-finding review process.
Correction safeguards depend on the source-grounded comparison and receipt rules.
The authorized replacement is the workflow described in the same engineering guidance.
Pruning preserves unfinished work and its cumulative budget, consistent with whole-operation accounting.
Evidence-backed closure remains subordinate to Markdown as documentary authority.
The ask procedure implements the bounded, resumable consultation contract.
The complexity limits depend on the selected analyzer and its per-function scoring method.
Source listing and reading help recover settled knowledge before asking the owner, as stated in the product purpose.
Relocation is permitted only when the old and destination paths satisfy the configured source-selection rules.
Only a context-paused check in an ask depends on that ask’s shared update/check/answer allowance; this remains ask-scoped.
Comparison feedback is reassessed against the source using source-fidelity criteria, not accepted as a verdict about the candidate.
Current retry/recovery rules remain constrained by the shared cumulative work budget.
Admission freshness checks must bind to an exact candidate snapshot whose format and integrity have been validated.
Within the former source-review workflow, source claims and results used the bounded review cohort store; this historical dependency does not make the store a current replacement-workflow obligation.
Supersession protects its record and replacement from pruning; pruning separately protects replacements referenced by supersession.
The approved Rust runtime replaces the initial TypeScript/Bun choice while retaining the product contract and cohesive modules.
Measured validation cost and bounded cases depend on exposing and preserving the work-wide consumption accounting.
A non-default profile transition depends on explicit continuation under the same work ID and scope; default-profile resumption remains automatic.
Development requires independent review and leaves acceptance to the principal reviewer.
Warning-change reporting depends on closure records and stale-evidence behavior.
The store-level attempt record and treatment of uncertain requests instantiate the broader invocation-accounting constraint.
The Clippy nesting threshold supplements the distinct project limit on function-local nesting.
Archive evidence selection remains governed by configured source selection, including exclusions overriding archive patterns.
Work validly superseded by a completed reviewed replacement is exempt from the ordinary import block for unfinished work.
The Rust migration retains cohesive domain modules, supporting the modular-monolith decision.
The portable skill operationalizes the product purpose.
The assessment's citation validation uses the documentary citation-matching rules, while code citations remain literal.
A review report is limited to the code and document versions it actually considered.
The explicit-update allowance applies whole-operation accounting without resetting consumption.
The selected package must be verified as the exact artifact prepared for publication.
Warning-change reporting depends on the current warning-maintenance and stale-evidence rules.
When resumed work invokes its profile, it depends on authenticated effective-profile validation and no silent fallback; this does not restrict zero-call profile recording.
The map's treatment of earlier ADRs as historical evidence supports preserving truthful status and replacement scope.
Codex invocation depends on effective-profile validation and explicit failure rather than fallback.
Archive handling preserves historical Markdown as evidence without elevating derived knowledge above documentary authority.
Profile changes preserve the operation-wide cumulative budget.
Import must preserve unfinished work and its attempts and budgets rather than bypassing its normal lifecycle.
The former cohort replacement depended on preserving and validating the prior review archive and retained rows.
Migration preservation includes cumulative budgets and usage under the operation-wide accounting contract.
Relocation must account for and preserve local work state, and refuses to proceed while that work is unfinished.
Resumable update rounds and checks remain within the operation-wide budget and retain its accounting.
The documented ownership map makes concrete the cohesive domain modules retained by the migration.
The replacement workflow no longer requires the former separate fidelity-cohort lifecycle; this does not erase its historical evidence.
The source-grounded engineering workflow supports the current product purpose at A10:9.
The scope of the complexity results depends on the stated limits of source analysis, particularly for macros.
Ingestion revision's reassociation of compatible source reviews uses the separate source-review operation.
The legacy-closure condition supports the current replacement-workflow decision and limits retirement to verified replacement.
A corrected proposal remains subject to current findings, valid evidence, and relationship-loss safeguards.
Current review binds reports to the code and Markdown versions considered, supporting ADR 0010:21. Do not map to the candidate requires edge with the same endpoints.
Freshness reporting keeps shared derived knowledge subordinate to its cited Markdown.
Revision requires a graph tied to the source plan, while graph snapshots are projections of complete verified cohorts with preserved provenance.
The documented Cargo-based tests and synthetic protocol tooling implement the Rust development-toolchain boundary.
Runner retirement remains conditional on a passing hosted workflow.
The Luna/max answer invocation depends on effective-profile validation and explicit failure behavior.
The Guide's current Codex protocol and effective-profile behavior is a concrete implementation of ADR 0013's replaceable integration contract.
Only the former mandatory candidate and fidelity admission ceremony is removed for the replacement workflow; the earlier decision remains a historical record.
Archive configuration enables focused access to historical sources without making them ordinary ingestion sources.
Version- and range-scoped consultation evidence implements the requirement to identify sources actually considered.
The rejected parallel installer machinery and independent-installation goal elaborate the earlier Bun product-stack choice.
Explicit non-default profile continuation preserves the same work and cumulative totals under ADR0010:23; recording a profile does not reset accounting.
A reviewed false-finding disposition cannot waive current candidate checks, relationship retention, or evidence validity.
Current Guide 42 decision b9e0de7d says the nested-ignore conflict blocks the initialization behavior in current Guide 40 decision 0f8e6022. Reuse both actual current roles for the exception-to edge.
Reuse is limited to new explicit updates; consultations, reviews, repairs, and retained work keep their existing paths.
The verifier must be run against the exact archive that is subject to inspection.
Bounded real cases and public-surface tests support the policy of protecting observable behavior and meaningful boundaries.
Supersession requires confirmed outcomes; acknowledgement of uncertain delivery cannot substitute for that evidence.
Treating prior interpretations as context rather than authority preserves the Markdown source-of-truth rule.
The mapping and removal paths implement the source-backed review contract for protected relationship findings.
Reopened-warning reporting depends on closure evidence and reactivation when sources become stale or unavailable.
Selection requires resolving actual blockers, for which the triage guidance distinguishes native dependencies and blocked or deferred work.
Safe retry requires preserving the prior receipt and attempt history.
A successful former pair comparison depended on complete validated claim and relationship assessments.
Behavioral and boundary testing supports the runtime migration's compatibility guarantees.
Repair compares derived interpretations against Markdown as the documentary authority.
A definitive claim-level verdict depends on complete coverage, scoped precedence handling and validated citations.
Initialization supplies the language-neutral base on which the principal agent completes project-specific purpose, vision, and language.
Supersession eligibility depends on identifiable coverage at source versions that remain current.
